text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000018 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation at every complexity level, but records came back for too few claims to tell whether the notes support the billing.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share holds within every condition-count band, not just among the sickest patients. A sizable minority of 99215s fall on patients with 0-1 conditions, for example C0008337 (low back pain only), C0008348 (hypertension only) and the Z09 follow-up visits C0008883 and C0008934. That pattern is consistent with upcoding rather than with a sicker panel alone. Against this, the 4 documented 99215 claims (e.g., C0008538, C0008837) all show high MDM with substantial minutes, and no documented claim fell below its billed level. But 4 charts is far too thin a sample to judge, and the 3 notes that claim moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim are weak evidence that documentation may be inflated or cloned. A reviewer should first obtain records for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims listed above and check whether the MDM documented there is clinically plausible for the diagnoses billed. The reviewer should also compare those notes against the documented 99215s for templated or cloned language."}
